A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HyperGCT research and contain complete main texts and supplementary Sections 6–9. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison, including material relocated between pages.

before.justification: v1 reports original registration experiments, cross-dataset generalization tests, robustness analyses and ablations in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a comparison of model parameter counts in supplementary Table 19.

M1.justification: The hypergraph construction, convolution and update blocks, GF-NMS seeding, hypothesis generation and losses are unchanged. The new inductive-bias discussion explains existing components rather than modifying the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use 3DMatch, 3DLoMatch, KITTI-10m, KITTI-LC and ETH with the same registration and generalization scenarios. The transformer-generated correspondence evaluations were already present in v1.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators, including the backend, hypothesis-generation and supplementary comparisons. New Table 19 reports parameter counts for the five learning-based comparators already evaluated; the newly cited papers are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Table 8 changes one reported compatibility-threshold setting from 0.58 to 0.85 while retaining its result entries. This is a reported setting correction, without evidence that experiments were rerun. Dataset splits, training settings, registration metrics and other evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Supplementary Section 7 adds a model-complexity analysis comparing parameter counts alongside existing runtime results. The graph-quality, threshold-sensitivity, update-frequency, backend, seeding and graph-order analyses are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random-seed schedules, confidence intervals or significance tests. The revision introduces no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: New Table 19 reports parameter counts of 1.05M for PointDSC, 0.96M for PG-Net, 3.25M for VBReg, 0.01M for Hunter and 0.27M for 3DPCP, alongside HyperGCT's already reported 0.98M. Existing registration scores, ablation outcomes and qualitative registration examples remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–18 retain their substance. The positive-part notation receives a cosmetic correction, and the new inductive-bias discussion adds no formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims of a dynamic-hypergraph geometric constraint, strong registration performance, robustness to graph noise and cross-dataset generalization. Wording edits do not substantively change these claims.

C2.justification: Supplementary Section 7 adds explanations connecting robustness and generalization to geometric priors, shared graph updates and progressively reduced vertex–hyperedge associations. It also argues that performance justifies model complexity. The GF-NMS failure limitation remains, although its separate label is removed.

D1.justification: v1's promise that code will be released is replaced by a concrete repository link in v2's first-page footnote. Comparative parameter counts are newly disclosed, while training hyperparameters, hardware and supplementary implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cheng et al.'s 'Sampling locally, hypothesis globally' and Yang et al.'s '3D registration in 30 years: A survey' to the citations. The broader positioning against traditional registration, learned correspondence filtering and static hypergraphs remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized edits to the abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion, adds two supplementary discussion paragraphs and acknowledgments, and shortens affiliations while adding email addresses. The overall section structure and most technical prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the parameter-count table and renumbers the dataset-information table from 19 to 20. Figures 2–3 and several existing tables move to earlier pages, with shortened captions and local layout adjustments. The pipeline graphic and supplementary registration visualizations retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves transparency and clarity through a concrete code location, the Table 8 threshold correction, and a parameter-count comparison supporting its complexity discussion. The added architectural rationale helps explain the existing design, while the method and empirical validation remain essentially unchanged.
